title: Single-crystal structural phase diagram of stoichiometric bilayer nickelate La3Ni2O7 under hydrostatic pressure
authors: Misaki Sasaki, Zhehong Liu, Takeshi Hara, Shunsuke Kitou, Markus Kriener, Haruto Yoshimochi, Shion Yamada, Chieko Terakura, Naohisa Hirao, Hirokazu Kadobayashi, Yusuke Wakabayashi, Yoshinori Tokura, Yasujiro Taguchi, Taka-hisa Arima, Yukako Fujishiro
abstract: The bilayer nickelate La3Ni2O7 has attracted intense interest following the discovery of high-temperature superconductivity under pressure, representing the first nickelate superconductor realized in bulk form. However, the crystal structure of the superconducting phase remains under active discussion, complicating efforts to establish its microscopic origin. Here we resolve these structural controversies by establishing a definitive pressure-temperature phase diagram, including the superconducting region of stoichiometric La3Ni2O7 single crystals under hydrostatic conditions using helium as the pressure-transmitting medium. At ambient pressure, La3Ni2O7 adopts a polar orthorhombic Am2m structure characterized by charge order between inequivalent Ni sites and NiO6 octahedral tilting. Upon compression, the system undergoes a direct transition from the charge-ordered Am2m phase to the tetragonal I4/mmm phase near 10 GPa, coinciding with the onset of bulk superconductivity. These results establish the intrinsic structural evolution of La3Ni2O7 and provide a structural framework for microscopic theories of nickelate superconductivity.
summary: This experimental study maps the structural phase diagram of bilayer nickelate La3Ni2O7 under high pressure using single-crystal X-ray diffraction. It definitively shows that superconductivity emerges precisely when the crystal structure undergoes a transition from an ambient orthorhombic phase to a tetragonal I4/mmm phase near 10 GPa. These findings provide crucial structural constraints for developing microscopic theories of nickelate superconductivity.
main_problem: The study aims to establish the definitive pressure-temperature phase diagram of stoichiometric bilayer nickelate La3Ni2O7 to resolve structural controversies complicating efforts to understand its microscopic origin of superconductivity.
main_result: A direct structural transition is observed from a polar orthorhombic Am2m phase at ambient pressure to a tetragonal I4/mmm phase near 10 GPa, which coincides with the onset of bulk superconductivity.
method: High-pressure single-crystal X-ray diffraction measurements were performed using a Diamond Anvil Cell (DAC) under hydrostatic conditions with helium as the pressure medium.
model_or_system: The physical system is stoichiometric bilayer nickelate La3Ni2O7. The investigation tracks structural changes, including octahedral tilting patterns and charge order, across varying pressures and temperatures.
key_observables: Crystal structure symmetry (Am2m vs I4/mmm), lattice parameters, and the appearance/disappearance of specific X-ray reflections ($h=2n+1$).
important_parameters: Pressure (up to 17.7 GPa) and Temperature (low T measurements at 9 K). The superconducting transition occurs near 10 GPa.
main_assumptions: The use of single, stoichiometric crystals under strictly hydrostatic conditions is assumed to provide a definitive structural picture, ruling out previous conflicting models.
figures_summary: Figures detail the pressure-temperature phase diagram showing superconductivity onset and diffraction patterns illustrating the orthorhombic to tetragonal symmetry change across the critical pressure region.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the experimental methodology using DAC/XRD on single crystals, presents evidence for the ambient $	ext{Am}2	ext{m}$ structure, maps out the structural transition ($	ext{Am}2	ext{m} 	o 	ext{I}4/	ext{mmm}$) coinciding with superconductivity onset, and concludes by providing a structural framework for theory.
why_interesting: The work directly probes the interplay between crystal symmetry breaking (structural phase transitions) and unconventional superconductivity in a strongly correlated nickelate material, which is highly relevant to understanding pairing mechanisms in cuprates and related systems.
